A studio that thinks in systems

Six people, a lot of half-finished sketches, two pen plotters, and a stubborn belief that the most interesting images are the ones nobody drew on purpose.

01 / Philosophy

We tune rules,
not pixels.

Noisewright started in 2017 as a shared studio between a computational designer and a sound artist who kept arguing about whether code could have a hand. Nine years later we have stopped arguing — it can, and the hand is mostly in the editing.

We don't sit down to draw a picture. We build a small machine with a few dials, set it running, and watch. Most of what it produces is forgettable. But somewhere in that space of possibility is the piece that is better than anything we could have composed by hand — and our entire job is to find it, name the conditions that made it, and lock the seed.

That means the deliverable is rarely a single file. It's a system: a renderer, a parameter range, a palette grammar, and a clear understanding of what makes a frame "ours." We hand clients living things, and we teach them to keep them alive.

02 / Process

How a piece gets made

Interrogate the brief

Before any code, we find the dataset, the constraint, or the feeling that should drive the system. A good generative piece always has a source of honest variation — tides, traffic, sound, a hash. We figure out yours.

Sketch in code

We prototype fast and ugly, dozens of quick renderers in an afternoon. The goal isn't beauty yet — it's discovering which family of algorithm has the right energy. Flow field? Tiling? Particle system? Reaction-diffusion?

Build the dials

Once a direction earns its keep, we expose its parameters as real controls — exactly like the lab on our home page. Clients drive the system themselves and learn its personality before we commit.

Curate & lock

We generate at volume and curate ruthlessly, fixing seeds, palettes, and ranges. For editions we set the rules of legitimacy; for installs we set the rules of behaviour.

Ship & sustain

Our installs are built to run unattended for years — watchdogs, graceful fallbacks, and a static frame for when motion isn't welcome. We hand over documentation a future maintainer can actually read.

03 / The team

Six humans, one machine

Each portrait is a deterministic generative mark — no two are alike.

Marta Valente

Founder · Computational design

Trained as an architect, defected to code in 2015. Obsessed with tiling, lattices, and the moment a system stops being legible.

Diogo Reis

Founder · Sound & interaction

Makes the work listen. Builds the sensor pipelines and real-time audio analysis behind our reactive installs.

Aïsha Bello

Creative technologist

Our shader specialist. Lives in GLSL, ports our heaviest CPU sketches to the GPU, and somehow keeps everything at 60fps.

Tomás Coelho

Plotter & fabrication

Keeps two AxiDraws and a CNC router alive. Turns our pixels into ink, aluminium, and the occasional 3-metre relief.

Lena Hofer

Producer

The reason installs ship on time and budgets close. Translates between artists, electricians, and very nervous museum directors.

Sam Okafor

R&D & open source

Maintains Quiet Engine and runs our workshops. Believes a good library is the most generous thing a studio can make.
